title: NAB joins other big banks to report a steep decline in mortgage lending
full_text:
Australia’s housing rout continues with National Australia Bank reporting a 15 per cent fall in its mortgage lending as borrowers retreat after Labor’s unpopular tax changes.
The banking major also warned trading will worsen, with credit growth set to turn negative in 2027 NAB, Australia’s biggest business lender, said its commercial customers would probably face a different story, with business borrowing continuing to rise.
Ruling off its third quarter results with cash profit up 2 per cent to $1.83bn, NAB said it was focusing on its lending margins, which slipped 2 basis points, amid hot competition for loans and deposits.
Its household lending rose $7bn over the June quarter, with home mortgages hitting $451bn, despite a 14 per cent fall in borrowing by homeowners, coupled with a 17 per cent slide in lending to investors.
Every major lender has revealed a slump in new borrowing in the wake of changes to negative gearing and capital gains discounts. Westpac is the biggest loser, with lending applications down 20 per cent. Commonwealth Bank has reported a 15 per cent drop, and ANZ is down 12 per cent.
NAB expects housing credit growth to be muted in 2027, tracking at just 2.5 per cent. Investor credit growth will turn negative in 2027, resulting in a 1.4 per cent contraction.
Chief executive Andrew Irvine said that despite the slide, his bank had grown in line with the rest of the banking market. He also pointed to the business arm, which saw lending up 4 per cent. “The combined impacts of the Middle East conflict, higher domestic interest rates and recent tax changes in the federal budget are creating challenges and uncertainties for our customers,” Mr Irvine said.
